A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRPO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original DRPO fine-tuning experiments on mathematical reasoning, including accuracy, response lengths, training dynamics, AES scores, and generated-response case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds Llama-8B results, K&K logic-puzzle experiments, and a reward-design ablation.

M1.justification: The default DRPO objective, positive-group normalization, KL constraint, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 adds evaluated concave and cosine reward variants alongside the original linear reward, changing reward-dependent training weights only in those variants.

E1.justification: V1 trains and evaluates exclusively on mathematical reasoning. V2 retains that coverage and adds K&K logic-puzzle training and evaluation in Appendix A.4, extending the empirical scope to a distinct non-mathematical reasoning task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched original experiments: RLOO-LP, ALP, HAPO, L1-MAX, ShorterBetter, and LASER-D remain represented. The new 8B and logic-puzzle comparisons use the already evaluated RLOO-LP, ALP, and HAPO methods; explicitly identifying existing reference settings as DisCO or GRPO does not add comparators.

E3.justification: The original mathematical evaluation protocol is retained. Added settings include DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B with learning rate 5e-7, and a 1.5B logic-puzzle protocol training on 3–7-person puzzles, testing on 2–8-person puzzles, training for 400 steps, and evaluating every 80 steps.

E4.justification: V2 adds a focused 1.5B mathematical-reasoning ablation comparing linear, concave, and cosine length rewards across three lambda values (Appendix A.5, Figure 6). Existing lambda sensitivity, difficulty analyses, illustrative advantage calculations, and case studies are retained; the latter are renumbered rather than replaced.

E5.justification: Both versions report Pass@1 averaged over 16 generated answers per prompt. Neither reports independent training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original 1.5B/7B results, including Tables 4–5, are retained. New 8B results include DRPO Pass@1 0.690, length 1758, and AES 0.297 versus RLOO-LP AES 0.251 (Table 1). The new logic experiment reports length decreasing from 2095 to 1400 with accuracy changing from 0.972 to 0.974. Reward-variant findings are also added; these are new experimental results, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 newly defines concave and cosine length rewards as 1-(|o|/C)^2 and 0.5+0.5 cos(pi|o|/C). The main mathematical framework, assumptions, closed-form optimal distribution, and Appendix A.1 derivation remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and central conclusion retain the same claims: composite rewards can misdirect GRPO, DRPO decouples positive and negative learning signals, and its tractable objective improves the accuracy–length trade-off. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new reward ablation as favoring linear rewards for a broader trade-off range and other shapes for higher accuracy at longer lengths. It qualifies baseline AES negativity from all to almost all, consistent with positive 8B RLOO-LP results. The conclusion removes v1's explicit computational limitation to 1.5B/7B models.

D1.justification: V2 documents the added 8B learning rate, logic-puzzle training/test composition and evaluation schedule, and alternative reward formulas with their lambda grid. Existing implementation details, pseudocode, and code-access information are retained; no new hardware or runtime information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused discussion of discriminative learning, including Lyu et al., Bai et al., and Su et al., distinguishing their binary-reward focus from DRPO's efficiency objective. V2 also adds GRPO-refinement and logic-task references and removes Liu et al. (2025c). The central positioning relative to GRPO and DisCO remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged. V2 adds a related-work paragraph, two appendix subsections, an LLM-writing-assistance disclosure, and localized experimental/discussion edits. Citation conventions, headings, author-contact presentation, and publication-header text also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR document layout, expands Figure 3 to three model panels, Figure 4 to three model rows, and Table 1 with an 8B group. It adds Figures 5–6 and Table 6 and relocates Algorithm 1. Original case-study Figures 5–7 become Figures 7–9 with their content retained.

improvement.justification: The Llama-8B evaluation, K&K experiment, and reward-shape ablation provide useful additional checks of model/task generalization and reward-choice sensitivity while retaining the original evidence. The baseline AES discussion also becomes better qualified. These are bounded empirical improvements: uncertainty reporting remains absent, and removing the explicit model-scale limitation slightly weakens transparency about the remaining scope.
